peak_demand_note: 15% of a 20B run = 3.0B; §2.1 requires the pool to hold >= 3x that = 9.0B minimum, and states the pool as 14B
method_note: The datasets-server /rows + /statistics quota is PER-IP, not per-account (verified by the
orchestrator: authenticated and anonymous both 429 in 0.1s with 13 concurrent recount.py
processes on one machine). All recount.py runs were stopped on instruction. Only ONE
recount.py run completed before the stop: finewiki/en.
For the two Wikipedia-derived sources the primary number here is NOT recount.py's
stats-ratio estimate. It is a stronger measurement obtained a different way:
PARQUET FOOTER BYTES x sampled tokens/byte. A parquet footer carries
total_uncompressed_size per column chunk, so summing it over every row group of every file
gives the EXACT total byte size of the `text` column over the WHOLE split -- the same
quantity num_rows x mean_chars estimates, but measured instead of sampled. This removes the
heavy-tailed factor from the estimate entirely; only tokens/byte (CV 0.166 per document) is
sampled. It also routes around the two defects in the finewiki recount.py result: its
/statistics mean was PARTIAL (421,456 of 6,614,655 rows = 6.4%, head of the split) and its
two estimators diverged 32%, which the tool correctly self-reported as confidence=low.
Footer reads go to the HUB CDN by ranged request, a different service and quota from
datasets-server, and moved ~1 MB against a 37 GB corpus. Still metadata-only: no
load_dataset(), no hf_hub_download of a data file. Tool at /tmp/footer_bytes.py.

sources.card_tokens_note: THE CARD NAMES NO TOKEN COUNT AND NO TOKENIZER. The design doc §3.2's '~3.5B' for this source has no traceable origin on the card; the card states only 35.1 GB / 6,614,655 pages for `en`. The '~3.5B' figure is off by ~2.5x and should be struck.
sources.confidence_note: num_rows exact (6,614,655) and text-column bytes EXACT (40,630,233,930 uncompressed, summed over 6,622 row groups in 15 files). Only tokens/byte is sampled: 0.21819 from 140 docs, per-doc tokens/char CV 0.166. Sensitivity: tok/byte 0.21 -> 8.53B, 0.23 -> 9.34B. So 8.5-9.3B, call it ~8.9B.

text_column_trap_measured.note: TRAP CONFIRMED QUANTITATIVELY, and avoided. recount.py chose `text` by known-name and stats_text_column() also preferred `text`. Counting `wikitext` would have inflated this by 1.64x to ~14.6B -- which would have falsely made the 14B pool look exactly met by this source alone. The dataset also ships an `infoboxes` string column (3.03 GB) that is metadata, not prose.

recount_py_result_for_comparison.confidence_note: estimators disagree by 32% and the /statistics mean is PARTIAL (head of the split, may be content-clustered)
recount_py_result_for_comparison.note: The footer measurement 8.87B falls BETWEEN this low-confidence pair (6.52B sample-mean, 9.58B partial-stats-ratio), which is the expected result if the partial /statistics head is biased toward longer articles -- it is: stats mean_chars 6,614.8 vs the random sample's 4,502.4. Exact bytes give mean 6,142.5 bytes/row, closer to the stats head than the small sample, so the sample was the noisier of the two.

sources.note: Aug 2025 HTML dumps, 325 languages, templates rendered, math + tables retained, citation sections removed. 2.07x the text bytes of wikimedia/wikipedia 20231101.en for 1.03x the pages -- the extraction is genuinely richer, not just newer.

sources.confidence_note: num_rows exact (6,407,814) and text bytes EXACT (19,621,046,728 over 6,437 row groups in 41 files). tokens/byte 0.21819 is BORROWED from the finewiki sample rather than sampled here (no datasets-server budget). Same script and domain, so the transfer is sound, but this corpus strips tables and math, which slightly lowers real tok/byte. Treat as +-10%.
sources.note: DO NOT SUM WITH FINEWIKI -- same articles, and finewiki explicitly supersedes it. Strictly worse for this pool: half the text bytes, tables and math removed, Nov 2023 vs Aug 2025. Listed only to quantify the overlap.

sources.confidence_note: 57.4 UTF-8 GB is a CARD figure x a tok/byte borrowed from finewiki. Needs a real count. Also: datasets-server /size reports partial=True for this repo (1,016,996 of 16.3M rows converted), so its viewer row count is NOT the corpus size -- do not size from the viewer.
sources.note: March 2025 dumps of EIGHT English Wikimedia projects: Wikipedia, Wikinews, Wikibooks, Wikiquote, Wikisource, Wikiversity, Wikivoyage, Wiktionary -- plus TALK pages. Overlaps finewiki on the Wikipedia portion only; the other seven projects and the talk pages are genuinely NEW reference text. The non-Wikipedia remainder is the single largest defensible ADDITION to this pool, but it needs a count and a Wikipedia-portion exclusion before it can be sized.

sources.license: mixed per-document: CC BY, CC BY-SA, or public domain (in metadata.license); observed rows CC BY-SA 3.0
sources.share_alike_note: PARTIALLY share-alike -- the collection is a per-document license mix, so an SA/non-SA split is a metadata filter, not a whole-corpus decision.
sources.note: ~330,000 NON-Wikimedia MediaWiki wikis (heavily Fandom) archived by Wikiteam to the Internet Archive, as of Sept 2024. ZERO overlap with Wikipedia -- the only large wiki-shaped source here that is genuinely independent of the Wikipedia lineage. Quality caveat: the sampled rows are fan wikis about web novels and Fandom template/doc pages, which is reference-SHAPED but not encyclopedic; the card also warns of license laundering. 13.7 GB over 26.9M docs = ~509 bytes/doc, i.e. mostly stubs.

sources.license: mixed per-page in metadata.license: CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC-SA, public domain
sources.share_alike_note: Third SA source alongside FineWiki and StackExchange. A parallel agent measured 32% of its rows as share-alike. Filter on metadata.license; do not assume uniformity (§7 item 2).
sources.note: Mirrors OpenStax books plus much else. Textbook prose, the highest-quality reference text in this list per token -- but only ~0.8B, so it is a quality contribution, not a pool filler.

sources.license: mixed per-document: CC BY / CC BY-SA / public domain
sources.note: Open textbooks. Too small to matter for sizing (~0.13B).

sources.note: 1,406 essays / 7 MB. NEGLIGIBLE -- ~0.0015B, four orders of magnitude below the pool. Named in the task as a candidate; it is not one.

sources.confidence_note: 661.1 GB is a card figure. Even at +-30% this is ~100-190B, i.e. 7-13x the whole pool on its own. Also /size partial=True (110,709 of 17.0M rows converted) -- the viewer row count is 0.65% of the corpus.
sources.note: US patent grants and applications. LARGEST single non-share-alike option by an order of magnitude and it ALONE can fill 14B ten times over. The real question is domain fit, not size: patent prose is technical, formulaic, legally hedged, and heavily boilerplate-repetitive -- it is reference-like in register but nothing like an encyclopedia. RECOMMEND as a bounded slice (a few B) to make the pool licence-diverse, NOT as the pool's backbone. Cheap to slice: the pool needs a few percent of it.

Full common-pile author listing enumerated (62 repos). These are the remaining collections large enough to matter, all public domain / non-SA, all card-derived. pre_1929_books (10.1B, 46.3 GB) is the standout: real long-form encyclopedic and scholarly prose, no share-alike, and it alone nearly fills the pool. Its cost is that the text is pre-1929, so factually stale -- fine for language modelling, wrong for anything knowledge-current. doab (open-access academic books) belongs to the academic category, not this one -- do not double-count it against another agent's pool.

category_total_measured_note: 8.87B is the ONLY high-confidence measured number in this category: finewiki/en. Everything else is card-derived and explicitly not measured.

meets_3x_peak_demand_detail.verdict: FAILS, but only just, and only from the source the design doc names. finewiki/en measures 8.87B against a 9.0B 3x floor -- 1.5% short. The doc's stated 14B pool is NOT reachable from finewiki/en alone; the doc's own '~3.5B' for that source is itself wrong (2.5x low).

pool_shortfall_note: THE GAP IS REAL BUT SMALLER THAN THE DESIGN DOC IMPLIES, AND IT IS CLOSEABLE.
1. The doc's own figure for its primary source is wrong. §3.2 says finewiki en '~3.5B'. The
card names no token count at all; measured under dolma2 from exact column bytes it is
~8.87B (8.5-9.3B). So the pool starts 2.5x better provisioned than the doc believed, and
the 14B target was never as far away as it looked.
2. English-only, share-alike-only, it still does not reach 14B. 8.87B is 63% of the pool and
1.5% short of the 9.0B 3x floor. As a single-source pool this fails, marginally.
3. The largest defensible ENGLISH pool, and what it is made of. Three tiers:
a. finewiki/en                       ~8.9B   MEASURED, high confidence   CC-BY-SA (SA)
b. common-pile/wikimedia_filtered    ~12.5B card, of which the SEVEN NON-Wikipedia
projects (Wikibooks, Wikisource, Wikiquote, Wikiversity, Wikivoyage, Wiktionary,
Wikinews) plus talk pages are new text. Even at a conservative one-third non-Wikipedia
that is ~4B of genuinely additive reference prose.       CC-BY-SA (SA)
c. common-pile/wikiteam_filtered     ~3.0B card, ZERO Wikipedia overlap, non-Wikimedia
wikis, mixed CC-BY / CC-BY-SA / PD.                      partly SA
(a)+(b non-Wikipedia)+(c) ~= 16B, which CLEARS 14B -- but it is almost entirely
share-alike, which collides head-on with §7 item 4's separability requirement: a 14B pool
that is ~90% SA is not 'kept separable from the rest of the corpus', it IS the corpus for
this category.
4. A 14B pool with a NON-share-alike backbone is also available, from public domain only:
pre_1929_books 10.1B + project_gutenberg 4.4B          = 14.5B  (long-form prose, stale)
library_of_congress 7.8B + usgpo 7.9B                  = 15.7B  (gov/archival)
uspto 144B                                             = 10x the pool by itself
All card figures, all public domain, none share-alike. So 14B IS reachable without any
share-alike source at all -- just not with encyclopedic, knowledge-current text.
5. RECOMMENDATION. Do not try to fill 14B from one lineage. Publish the reference pool as two
labelled, separable partitions:
reference-sa   ~9B   finewiki/en (+ wikimedia_filtered non-Wikipedia projects if counted)
reference-pd   ~5B   pre_1929_books and/or project_gutenberg and/or a uspto slice
That hits 14B, satisfies §7 item 4 by construction rather than by promise, and keeps the
SA obligation confined to a partition a consumer can exclude with a label filter. Per
MEMORY 'mixture cannot span groups', these must be values of the `source` label inside ONE
group, not separate groups, or build_mixture cannot draw across them.
6. IF 14B MUST COME FROM ENCYCLOPEDIC TEXT ONLY, IT DOES NOT EXIST under a redistributable
license in English. The honest ceiling is ~9B (finewiki/en) plus whatever the
wikimedia_filtered non-Wikipedia projects actually measure. Options then are: cut the pool
to 9B (still 3x a 15% peak of a 20B run, i.e. exactly adequate), or accept multilingual.
7. MULTILINGUAL IS AVAILABLE BUT OFF-MISSION. finewiki ships 325 configs, 184.7 GB total vs
35.1 GB for `en` -- so ~5.3x the English text, i.e. roughly 45B tokens all-languages, which
fills 14B three times over. The reservoir is English-centric, so this would change the
corpus's language distribution, not just its size, and it should be a deliberate decision
rather than a sizing convenience. Note the row counts mislead here: `ceb` (Cebuano) is the
2nd-largest config by ROWS (5.6M) but only 4.4 GB, because it is bot-generated stubs.
overlaps: HuggingFaceFW/finewiki en vs wikimedia/wikipedia 20231101.en -- SAME ARTICLES, near-total overlap. DO NOT SUM. Measured: finewiki holds 2.07x the text bytes (40.63 GB vs 19.62 GB) for 1.03x the pages, because it renders templates and retains tables and math that wikimedia/wikipedia strips. finewiki strictly supersedes it; wikimedia/wikipedia should not enter the pool at all.

common-pile/wikimedia_filtered CONTAINS English Wikipedia (March 2025) -- overlaps finewiki en on the Wikipedia portion. Its other seven Wikimedia projects and its talk pages do NOT overlap. Summing it whole with finewiki double-counts Wikipedia twice; only the non-Wikipedia remainder is additive.
common-pile/wikiteam_filtered is NON-Wikimedia wikis -- no overlap with either Wikipedia source. It is the one genuinely independent wiki lineage available.
wikimedia/structured-wikipedia (enwiki_namespace_0, 7.6M rows, 37.2 GB parquet, CC-BY-SA 4.0) is a THIRD view of English Wikipedia. Same overlap hazard; adds nothing finewiki lacks.
common-pile/libretexts_filtered MIRRORS OpenStax books -- if OpenStax is ingested directly (design doc §7) it will overlap libretexts. Dedupe or pick one.
common-pile/doab_filtered (open-access academic books, 2.6B) is claimed by the ACADEMIC category, not this one -- do not count it in both pools.

common-pile/project_gutenberg_filtered and common-pile/pre_1929_books_filtered are both public-domain pre-1929 book scans from overlapping provenance (Gutenberg texts appear in mass-digitization corpora). Treat their sum as an upper bound, not a total.
needs_streaming_count: common-pile/wikimedia_filtered -- the most important one to count: the non-Wikipedia-project remainder is the largest defensible addition to this pool and is currently a card figure. /size is partial=True (1.0M of 16.3M rows), so the viewer cannot substitute. Needs a per-project (metadata.source) breakdown, not just a total.
common-pile/wikiteam_filtered -- 2.99B card-derived; also needs a per-document license histogram to size the CC-BY vs CC-BY-SA split.
common-pile/uspto_filtered -- 144B card-derived, /size partial=True (0.65% converted). Only a bounded slice matters, so an exact total is low priority; a domain-fit sample matters more.
common-pile/libretexts_filtered -- 0.79B card-derived; needs the metadata.license histogram anyway for §7 item 2 (a parallel agent has 32% SA).

common-pile/pre_1929_books_filtered and project_gutenberg_filtered -- 10.1B and 4.4B card-derived; these are the non-SA backbone candidates, so they should be counted before the two-partition plan is committed.
common-pile/pressbooks_filtered, oercommons_filtered, public_domain_review_filtered -- card-derived, but all three are <=0.13B and cannot change the sizing verdict. Lowest priority.
HuggingFaceFW/finewiki non-English configs -- only if multilingual is accepted. The footer-bytes method makes this cheap (~1 MB per config) and does not touch datasets-server.

NOTE ON METHOD: every item above is countable EXACTLY by the parquet-footer route (/tmp/footer_bytes.py) wherever a parquet conversion exists, with no datasets-server quota at all. common-pile/comma_v0.1_training_dataset holds the filtered mixture per-source, but as .json.gz/.jsonl.gz, not parquet, so footers do not apply there; common-pile/raw_v0.1_parquet does have parquet per-source folders and is the right target.
